subject: Hosted API evaluation — next steps & rate limits
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie@acme-retail.com>, procurement@acme-retail.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API evaluation — next steps & rate limits

Hi Jamie — great to meet earlier today, thanks for taking the demo. Quick recap and proposed next steps from my side: 

- Recap: We walked through the Hosted API (text generation, chat, embeddings), sample latency numbers on your sample prompt set, and the management console for usage/keys.
- Key decision: You mentioned wanting to validate whether Hosted API meets your latency/residency needs before considering Dedicated or Private.

Next steps I recommend for a Hosted evaluation:
1) Quickstart sandbox: I'll provision a short-lived test API key and sandbox endpoints so your team can run a subset of traffic (we typically recommend 1k-10k requests across representative prompts).
2) Test plan: If you can share a short prompt set and target SLO (p50 latency, p95, and tokens/sec), Marissa can help configure the tests and advise on batching/kv-cache.
3) Limits & scale: I'll attach a one‑page rate limits summary and our default concurrency/rate tiers. We can temporarily increase rates for evaluation.
4) Contract/procurement: Looping Rachel (CC) for PO/timeline questions — if Hosted looks good we can discuss a short-term pilot commit or monthly usage plan.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf (quickstart steps), hosted-api-rate-limits.csv (defaults).

Would you be able to share your top 10 prompts and ideal p95 latency target by end of day Friday? Also tell us whether data residency (EU/US) is a hard requirement for this evaluation.

Happy to set 30 min tomorrow for Marissa and your infra team to align on endpoints and observability if that helps.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Aditya Rao | aditya@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132
From: Jamie Liu <jamie@acme-retail.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation — next steps & rate limits

Thanks Aditya — useful recap. A few quick clarifying questions before we spin up tests: 

1) Data residency: For this initial eval our PII-scrubbed test traffic can stay in US regions, but production will likely need EU residency for a subset of flows. Does Hosted API support EU-region tenancy and separate keys?

2) Rate limits & concurrency: What are the sandbox default rate limits and burst allowances? We need to simulate peak traffic (~200 concurrent small requests, and occasional spikes to ~1k rps for short windows).

3) Endpoint types: Do you provide separate streaming vs non-streaming endpoints? Our client uses streaming for chat and non-streaming for batch scoring.

4) Cost guidance: Any ballpark cost per 1M tokens for the hosted models you demo'd? We can give you an internal estimate so procurement has numbers.

If you can provision a sandbox key and the quickstart steps, Marissa/your SE can coordinate with our infra. We can do a sync tomorrow 10:30am PT if that works.

Jamie Liu
Head of ML Engineering, Acme Retail
jamie@acme-retail.com

Thanks Jamie — answers inline below and next actions. Looping Marissa to schedule the infra sync and Rachel for procurement timeline.

1) Data residency: Yes — our Hosted API supports region-specific deployments. For evaluations we can provision a sandbox in the US; we can also spin a parallel EU sandbox if you want to validate residency constraints. Keys are scoped to region. For production, we offer EU-hosted tenants under our Enterprise plan.

2) Rate limits & concurrency: Attached is the hosted-api-rate-limits.csv with default tiers. For sandbox we typically set:
- Default single-key: 60 requests/sec (small requests) and 10 concurrent streaming connections.
- Burst/short-term increases: we can raise to 300 rps and 200 concurrent for a limited window during your test.
- For sustained peaks at 1k rps we recommend Dedicated or a burst agreement; Marissa can advise on autoscaling behavior.

3) Endpoints: We provide separate endpoints for streaming (server-sent events) and non-streaming (single response). Both endpoints support the same model catalog and rate limit enforcement.

4) Cost guidance: Ballpark hosted cost for the model shown in the demo is ~ $5–$12 per 1M tokens depending on quantization and throughput configuration; we'll provide a more precise estimate after we capture your token-size distribution.

Next actions:
- I'll provision a US sandbox API key (valid for 7 days) and share credentials + endpoint by EOD.
- Marissa: could you join a 30min sync tomorrow at 10:30am PT to align on test traffic and confirm whether we should enable a temporary higher rate window?
- Jamie/procurement: Rachel will follow up on sample contract length for a pilot commit and PO process.

Attachments: hosted-api-rate-limits.csv (current default tiers).

Thanks —
Aditya
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
